source_metadata.exact_title: Indigo Aspiration System for Treatment of Pulmonary Embolism: Results of the EXTRACT-PE Trial
source_metadata.source_type: Prospective single-arm multicenter investigational device trial

validation_report.duplicate_review: No exact duplicate canonical statements or source-anchor duplicates were identified in the generated set.
consistency_findings: The source reports both 98.3% avoiding intraprocedural tPA and 94.1% receiving no tPA through 48 hours; these refer to different time windows and were retained as distinct assertions.

extraction_limitations: This extraction captures study-defining eligibility, methods, key baseline characteristics, all principal efficacy and safety results, major limitations, funding, and conflicts; it does not atomize every non-load-bearing baseline table cell or every individual 30-day serious adverse-event diagnosis.
The supplementary appendix site-address table was inspected for multicenter provenance but site addresses were not atomized because they are administrative rather than study-claim assertions.

atoms.canonical_statement: EXTRACT-PE prospectively evaluated the safety and efficacy of the Indigo aspiration system for treatment of submassive acute pulmonary embolism.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study sought to prospectively evaluate the safety and efficacy of the Indigo aspiration system in submassive acute pulmonary embolism (PE).

atoms.canonical_statement: EXTRACT-PE was a prospective, single-arm investigational device exemption trial enrolling 119 patients at 22 U.S. sites.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: EXTRACT-PE ... was a single-arm investigational device exemption (IDE) trial that enrolled 119 patients at 22 U.S. sites.

atoms.canonical_statement: All investigational sites obtained Institutional Review Board approval and maintained IRB oversight through study completion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: all sites obtained Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval ... IRB oversight was maintained at each site through completion.

atoms.canonical_statement: An independent centralized imaging core laboratory measured CTA RV/LV ratios used for the primary efficacy analysis and measured clot burden with the Qanadli CT obstruction index.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A centralized imaging core lab ... performed a single-assessor analysis of CTA images ... Imaging Core Laboratory measurements were used for primary efficacy endpoint analysis. Additionally, the Imaging Core Laboratory measured clot burden using the Qanadli CT obstruction index.

atoms.canonical_statement: A Clinical Events Committee adjudicated reported adverse events for final safety analyses, superseding site assessments, and an independent Data Safety Monitoring Board reviewed aggregate safety data.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A Clinical Events Committee adjudicated reported adverse events ... superseded investigational site assessments for final safety endpoint analysis. atoms.canonical_statement: The protocol defined submassive PE as acute PE without systemic hypotension but with either right ventricular dysfunction or myocardial necrosis, using specified imaging, biomarker, and ECG criteria.

atoms.canonical_statement: The Indigo aspiration system consisted of an 8-F aspiration catheter, associated tubing, pump, and separator.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The Indigo aspiration system (Penumbra) is comprised of the 8-F Indigo aspiration catheter and its associated tubing, pump, and separator (Figure 2).

exposures.details: 8-F Indigo aspiration catheter with associated tubing, pump, and separator; sustained aspiration thrombectomy

atoms.canonical_statement: The procedure used sustained aspiration after advancing the catheter proximal to thrombus, with optional separator use and repeat aspiration in multiple pulmonary vessels.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Once proximal to the occlusive thrombus, the physician initiated sustained aspiration with the pump. If appropriate, the separator was advanced ... Aspiration could be repeated in multiple pulmonary vessels.

exposures.details: 8-F Indigo aspiration catheter with associated tubing, pump, and separator; sustained aspiration thrombectomy

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in RV/LV diameter ratio from baseline to 48 hours; success required the lower bound of the 95% CI for mean change to exceed 0.2.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary efficacy endpoint analysis was the difference between the baseline and the 48-h RV/LV diameter ratio... endpoint was met if the lower bound of the confidence interval was >0.2.

concept.text: Change in RV/LV diameter ratio from baseline to 48 hours

outcome.definition: Difference between baseline and 48-h RV/LV diameter ratio; endpoint met if lower 95% CI bound >0.2

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary safety endpoint was the 48-hour major adverse event rate, a composite of device-related death, major bleeding, and device-related serious adverse events; success required the upper 95% CI bound to be below 40%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary safety endpoint was the rate of major adverse events at 48 h, a composite of device-related death, major bleeding, and device-related serious AEs ... met if the upper bound of the CI was <40%.

outcome.definition: Composite of device-related death, major bleeding, and device-related serious adverse events

atoms.canonical_statement: Device-related serious adverse events comprised clinical deterioration, pulmonary vascular injury, and cardiac injury.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Device-related SAEs were a composite of clinical deterioration, pulmonary vascular injury, and cardiac injury.

outcome.definition: Composite of clinical deterioration, pulmonary vascular injury, and cardiac injury

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were assessed at baseline, during the procedure, at 48 hours, discharge, and 30 days; CTA was performed at baseline and 48 hours.
